text.p: Murata Mfg Co Ltd said on Thursday that it expects to post a parent current profit of about 26.6 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1997, up from its previous forecast of about 25.3 billion yen.
Its parent current profit was 30.21 billion yen in 1995/96.
"We now expect a larger profit due to robust sales of electronics parts since last autumn," a company spokesman said. Murata makes ceramic capacitors and electronic parts.
Murata forecast parent sales of about 254 billion yen in 1996/97, against its previous forecast of 252 billion yen and actual 1995/96 sales of 255.12 billion yen, the spokesman said.

He said, however, that Murata's group net profit in 1996/97 would be about 33 billion yen, unchanged from its previous forecast, due to a decline in prices for its products in overseas markets. It posted a group net profit of 37.24 billion yen in 1995/96.
The company sees group sales rising to about 332 billion yen in 1996/97, against actual group sales of 321.86 billion yen in the previous year.
By 0440 GMT, Murata's shares had risen 130 yen to 4,230 yen on the Osaka Securities Exchange.
